# APRS packet decoding and compliance test vectors

Edition 1 — prepared 2026-10-15. Source baseline: APRS Protocol Reference document 1.0.1, the live APRS 1.1 addendum and selected clarifications it links, and the pinned `hessu/go-aprs-fap` tests.

This document contains **1,545 numbered cases: 1,538 individual packet cases and 7 stateful sequences containing 23 additional packet occurrences**. There are 1,028 specification-derived, historical, policy, ambiguity, and robustness cases, plus 517 FAP compatibility snapshots. The individual cases contain 1,515 distinct byte strings. Repeated strings are intentional where profiles or parser options change the expected result.

Every packet is fully expanded. JSON strings preserve padding, backslashes, embedded colons, control bytes, and high-bit bytes. The decoded fields are intended as inputs to an implementation-neutral test adapter; the FAP appendix deliberately uses a separate schema. This is a broad finite corpus, not a claim that all possible APRS byte combinations, products, or later extensions have been enumerated.

## Sources and authority

`APRS101 p.N` always means the **printed page number**, not a PDF viewer page index. The supplied PDF has ten front-matter pages before printed page 1. Its cover identifies document version 1.0.1, dated 29 August 2000, describing protocol version 1.0.

| Label         | Source and use                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| A11 DF        | [Direction-finding notes](https://www.aprs.org/APRS-docs/DF.TXT), linked from the addendum; consulted 2026-10-15.                                                                         |
| A11 AREA      | [Area-object corrections](https://www.aprs.org/aprs11/areaobjects.txt), linked from the addendum; consulted 2026-10-15.                                                                   |
| A11 WX        | [Weather clarifications](https://www.aprs.org/aprs11/spec-wx.txt), linked from the addendum; consulted 2026-10-15.                                                                        |
| A11 REPLY-ACK | [Reply acknowledgment algorithm](https://www.aprs.org/aprs11/replyacks.txt), linked from the addendum; consulted 2026-10-15.                                                              |
| A11 names     | [Names and spaces](https://www.aprs.org/aprs11/aprs-names-and-spaces.txt), linked from the addendum; consulted 2026-10-15.                                                                |
| A11 Objects   | [Object ownership and lifecycle](https://www.aprs.org/aprs11/Objects.txt), linked from the addendum; consulted 2026-10-15.                                                                |
| A11 PHG       | [PHG range presentation](https://www.aprs.org/symbols/PHGmobile.txt), linked from the addendum; consulted 2026-10-15.                                                                     |

| FAP           | [Repository at the captured commit](https://github.com/hessu/go-aprs-fap/tree/94c7118ca94d251990382b9210112ddd5b260efa). Each compatibility case links to its exact source file and line. |

The supplied PDF SHA-256 is `78a72618c788b8b7f8369004884018f9b02f990069ff67915bb1e30738b1da01`. The FAP commit is **`94c7118ca94d251990382b9210112ddd5b260efa`**, dated 2026-10-13T22:45:03Z. The web addendum is a live page: its text includes updates later than the nominal July 2004 freeze. Here, `core-1.1` means the retrieved addendum applied to APRS101, not a reconstruction of the site as it existed in 2004. The web pages are identified by URL and consultation date; no immutable revision identifier was available.

Authority order: explicit addendum corrections; APRS101 grammar and tables where not corrected; a stated corpus convention where the sources leave a representation choice; FAP only for the separately labeled compatibility profile. Neither a FAP acceptance nor a FAP rejection establishes protocol conformance by itself.

<a id="contract"></a>

## How to consume the vectors

### Bytes and framing

1. Select a profile before evaluating results. Do not combine contradictory historical, disputed, and compatibility expectations into one mandatory test set.
2. Extract JSON code blocks containing an `id`. All such blocks are complete numbered cases. Other code blocks contain documentation or defaults.
3. Decode the JSON `packet` string, then encode it as **Latin-1, one byte per code point**. Latin-1 is a reversible byte carrier here, not a claim that APRS text uses an international character set. Encoding the JSON-decoded string as UTF-8 corrupts binary Mic-E and high-bit message fixtures.
4. Pass exactly those bytes to the parser, without trimming or adding CR/LF. These are monitor-format packets, normally `SOURCE>DEST[,PATH...]:INFORMATION`. No AX.25 flag, FCS, KISS framing, AX.25 control/PID octet, line timestamp, or terminating newline is included. One explicitly labeled AEA transport case uses AEA framing.
5. Map your parser output to the semantic schema below. Test packet parsing separately from retained station state, routing, archiving, and UI behavior.

```python
raw_packet = case["packet"].encode("latin-1")
assert len(raw_packet) == case["packet_length_bytes"]
if "packet_hex" in case:
    assert raw_packet == bytes.fromhex(case["packet_hex"])
```

`packet_hex` is additionally present whenever a single-packet fixture contains nonprintable or non-ASCII bytes. The JSON representation is sufficient for every fixture; hex is a second byte-level cross-check. Escapes such as `\u001c`, `\u007f`, and `\u00ff` each represent one byte after the Latin-1 conversion. Literal `...` or spaces inside a packet are real protocol characters, never an editorial omission.

### Semantic field contract

| Field or convention                    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `header.source`, `header.destination`  | Raw outer address text, preserving explicit SSIDs and case. This is separate from a library's address normalization.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `header.path`                          | Ordered path components. `repeated_marker` records an actual trailing `*`; it does not infer earlier hops' H bits. APRS-IS q tokens are not RF AX.25 callsigns.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `kind` / `format`                      | Semantic packet category / position encoding. A weather-bearing object retains `kind: object` and contains weather fields. Query, bulletin, and telemetry-definition categories are useful refinements of the APRS message container.                                                                                     |
| Position                               | Signed decimal degrees, north/east positive, using WGS-84 unless explicitly noted. Compressed expected coordinates are the decoded, quantized values.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Ambiguity                              | `ambiguity_digits` is 0–4. `cell_bounds_deg` carries the transmitted area; the scalar coordinate is its center by corpus convention. Bounds are ascending numeric endpoints, including west/south cases. They do not imply an exact station fix.                                                                          |
| Symbols                                | Retain `table_id_raw`, normalized primary/alternate table, symbol `code`, and overlay. In compressed positions, `a`–`j` mean numeric overlays 0–9. The corpus tests encoding, not current icon artwork or the entire live symbol registry.                                                                                |
| Timestamps                             | Preserve raw bytes and transmitted components. UTC/local-zone labels do not supply missing year, month, day, local offset, or a receiver clock. Never invent a complete instant from a partial timestamp.                                                                                                                 |
| Motion                                 | Unit-suffixed names are explicit. Preserve course code 360 if transmitted; it is equivalent in direction to north but need not be normalized to 0. Uncompressed course code 000 can mean unavailable.                                                                                                                     |
| Altitude                               | `/A=` uses feet; compressed altitude uses logarithmically encoded feet; Mic-E altitude uses meters with a 10,000 m bias. GGA altitude is MSL and geoid separation is a separate field. No unsupported datum conversion is assumed.                                                                                        |
| Weather                                | Keep raw encoded measurements as well as named conversions. `null` means unavailable, not a measured zero. `p`, `P`, and `r` have distinct accumulation windows. Software/device strings do not create sensor readings.                                                                                                   |
| Objects and items                      | Keep both padded `name_raw` and the identity name with right-padding removed. Preserve case. A kill packet is a valid lifecycle update, not malformed position data.                                                                                                                                                      |
| Messages                               | Preserve the nine-byte `addressee_raw`, unpadded addressee, text, ID, and acknowledgment semantics. Message IDs are strings; leading zeros matter. Group addressing, bulletins, and NWS references have different acknowledgment rules.                                                                                   |
| Telemetry                              | Analog samples are raw channel values, ordered A1–A5. Digital characters are B1–B8 left to right. A missing channel is null, not zero. Calibration and bit-label sense require station-specific definition state.                                                                                                         |
| `comment`, `status_text`, raw payloads | Byte-preserving values after the recognized fields shown in the case are consumed. Removing parsed extension bytes can leave adjacent spaces; preserve those spaces. A parser may also expose the original unsliced comment.                                                                                              |
| Missing keys and `null`                | An absent optional semantic field means this packet supplies no assertion for that feature; do not manufacture an observation from absence. Explicit null asserts an unavailable value. Diagnostic metadata and additional correctly decoded fields are permitted. Sequence `expected` maps are partial state assertions. |
| `error_class`                          | A corpus-level diagnostic category, not a required exception message or exact parser API. Keep the envelope or other recoverable fields when appropriate.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `policy`, `position_usable`            | Application behavior assertions. A syntactically decodable but invalid NMEA fix must not become a trusted position update; network retention/routing flags belong to the policy layer.                                                                                                                                    |

Strings, raw codes, integer measurements, flags, and identifiers compare exactly. For converted floating-point values, use absolute tolerance `1e-8` degrees for coordinates and `1e-6` in the named physical unit, or relative tolerance `1e-9` where the magnitude warrants it. These tolerances cover decimal serialization and arithmetic differences; they do not excuse a wrong unit, an incorrect ambiguity cell, or comparing the encoder input against its quantized output. Negative zero and zero are numerically equivalent.

Exact conversions used: 1 knot = 1.852 km/h = 1852/3600 m/s; 1 mph = 0.44704 m/s; 1 statute mile = 1.609344 km; 1 foot = 0.3048 m; 1 inch = 25.4 mm; 1 hundredth inch = 0.254 mm; Celsius = (Fahrenheit − 32) × 5/9; 1 millibar = 1 hPa. Storm radii are nautical miles. A gauge datum is not inferred from a water-height number.

## Profiles and outcomes

| Profile                    | Cases | Purpose                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------- | ----: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `core-1.1`                 |   801 | APRS101 plus explicit live-addendum corrections; field decoding and selected application semantics.                             |
| `historical-1.0`           |    41 | Legacy behavior retained for deliberate backward compatibility; not a modern transmission recommendation.                       |
| `strict-envelope`          |    14 | RF/TNC2 transmitter and envelope constraints. Do not apply RF address restrictions indiscriminately to APRS-IS.                 |
| `strict-validation`        |   112 | Malformed fields, width/range limits, or a stated conservative extension-extraction policy. Valid surrounding data may survive. |
| `disputed-units`           |    12 | Uncompressed complete-weather wind has conflicting units in APRS101 and FAP. Choose a named interpretation.                     |
| `disputed-zero`            |     1 | All-zero complete-weather wind can represent unavailable data or measured calm, depending on the chosen policy.                 |
| `nmea-supported`           |    20 | Optional NMEA parsing capability. Raw fields and interpreted values are given; this is not a full NMEA standard suite.          |
| `linked-weather-extension` |     4 | Later water-gauge fields described in the addendum's linked weather notes.                                                      |
| `network-policy`           |     5 | No-gate and no-archive application behavior, separate from syntactic packet validity.                                           |
| `aprs-is`                  |     6 | Preserve Internet path tokens and case. Does not implement full q-construct server rules.                                       |
| `aea-transport`            |     1 | Historical monitor-format adapter; normalize to TNC2 before ordinary packet parsing.                                            |
| `opaque-vendor`            |     4 | Recognize vendor/raw-weather family and retain payload; supplied protocol sources do not fully define measurements.             |
| `stateful`                 |     7 | Ordered packets plus initial conditions and partial expected state after each step.                                             |
| `compatibility-fap`        |   517 | Captured results of a pinned implementation, including extensions, permissive behavior, and known discrepancies.                |

| Outcome           | Assertion                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `accept`          | The fields described by this profile decode. This alone does not authorize forwarding or transmission.            |
| `reject-envelope` | No valid outer RF/TNC2 envelope under the selected strict profile.                                                |
| `reject-field`    | A specified field is invalid; do not produce a trusted value for it. Whole-packet discard is not required.        |
| `reject-fix`      | Do not use this NMEA report as a position fix. Raw diagnostic fields may remain available.                        |
| `opaque`          | Classify and preserve without inventing a detailed decoder. Ignoring an unsupported payload safely is acceptable. |
| `reject`          | FAP returned an error in the captured compatibility run. This is not a normative APRS verdict.                    |

Stateful records have `steps` instead of a single `packet` and `outcome`. Reset state before each sequence, apply the stated initial condition, and evaluate the listed state assertions in order. The sequence vectors do not simulate RF transmission, timers, retransmission queues, or an interactive operator.

Verification performed while building this edition:

- Recovered **494 root-parser invocations** from the upstream tests, preserving each concrete packet byte string and parser-option set. Added **23 supplements** from encoder expectations, CLI fixtures, a log fixture, and the example. Their individual notes state any added envelope or removed log timestamp. The 517 compatibility rows contain 506 unique input byte strings.
- Ran the pinned upstream tests under Go 1.26.1 with a capture wrapper and unchanged assertions: **489 named test/subtest/example pass events**, no failed test events. This checks the original assertions; it does not independently certify every newly captured output field.
- Independently decoded the generated coordinate/movement/altitude data, including all 265 Mic-E packets, 335 non-Mic-E position packets, 26 area encodings, message address widths, and 29 applicable accepted NMEA checksums. The verifier performed **2,011 numeric comparisons**, with no failures. Correct-checksum invalid-fix packets were separately constructed to isolate fix status.
- Checked unique case IDs, finite numeric values, every individual packet's JSON/Latin-1 round trip, and all 23 sequence packet byte encodings. The final Markdown JSON records were extracted again and compared with the checked record data.

The FAP comparison is a second implementation check, not the source of the normative coordinate formulas. Several disagreements are retained deliberately and described below. Numeric validation cannot establish that every prose interpretation is correct; the ambiguity register makes the important judgment calls reviewable.

### Boundaries of this corpus

Binary AX.25 address/control/PID/FCS encoding, KISS framing, modem behavior, RF scheduling, digipeater algorithms, authenticated APRS-IS sessions, live TOCALL assignments, complete symbol artwork, UI geometry/rendering, and timing-dependent client behavior need separate suites. Generic NMEA variants beyond the sentences here need a NMEA specification. The external polygon/line format linked from the addendum and underdocumented vendor/Agrelo payload layouts need their own authoritative grammar before decoded numerical fields can be asserted. They are not silently treated as malformed APRS.

The FAP appendix exercises DAO, base-91 comment telemetry, relaxed telemetry, PHG variants, and weather extensions that exceed the historical APRS101 scope. Their inclusion is compatibility coverage, not a claim of complete APRS 1.2 coverage. Optional structured NTS decoding can be omitted while preserving the exact ordinary message text. Symbol overlay encoding cases do not assert that every historical client displays every overlay combination.

<a id="decisions"></a>

## Ambiguities and implementation differences

1. **Weather wind units.** APRS101 p.27 labels the uncompressed `ddd/sss` speed as knots; pinned FAP `weather.go` decodes it as mph. The `disputed-units` cases retain the raw speed and both named conversions. Select one contract; do not require two simultaneous physical wind speeds. Positionless `s` and gust `g` are explicitly mph. Compressed weather uses the compressed speed formula in knots and represents wind, not station movement. See [WX-002](#wx-002) and [WX-051](#wx-051). The supplied sources do not resolve the uncompressed discrepancy unambiguously.

2. **Unavailable versus zero.** APRS101 p.27 permits `000/000` for unknown or irrelevant movement, whereas receivers can use a numeric zero wind as measured calm. [WX-060](#wx-060) selects the unavailable interpretation only as a disputed profile. Dots/spaces are unambiguously unavailable. Never collapse missing humidity/rain/temperature into zero. `h00` means 100 percent humidity.

3. **Base-91 alphabet.** The radix is 91, so digits 0–90 map to ASCII 33–123 (`!` through `{`). APRS101 p.20's endpoint 124 (`|`) conflicts with that radix and later formulas. The corpus uses the actual base-91 arithmetic and rejects `|` as a compressed numeric digit. When compressed `c` is a space, the remaining `csT` data is ignored; the complete 13-byte layout is still required. See [CMP-005](#cmp-005).

4. **Area-object corrections.** The linked AREA correction supersedes p.60: offset degrees = code²/1500, and the transmitted coordinate is the lower reference point (circle center), not the upper offset-reference point. Thus code 10 gives 1/15 degree, not the one-degree prose example. Raw shape/color/offset codes remain testable even where ellipse/triangle rendering is underdescribed. The corpus does not assert a complete rendered polygon. See [OBJ-023](#obj-023).

5. **Mic-E byte ranges and optional data.** The A11 longitude erratum corrects the upper character endpoints on p.48. Mic-E is byte-sensitive and can contain control/DEL bytes. Its two-channel hexadecimal telemetry form transmits channels 1 and 3; the untransmitted channel 2 is null, not measured zero. Some FAP fixtures accept telemetry lengths outside p.54. Those remain compatibility cases. See [MIC-261](#mic-261).

6. **Mic-E ambiguity.** Latitude ambiguity also limits longitude precision. The area is the semantic result; this document uses its center for a deterministic scalar. FAP does not apply ambiguity consistently to both coordinates, so its captured coordinates differ for these cases. Do not replace the core expected cells with the FAP snapshot. See [MIC-236](#mic-236) through [MIC-239](#mic-239).

7. **Compressed object minimum length.** A minimal compressed object information field is 1 + 9 + 1 + 7 + 13 = 31 bytes. The pinned FAP object parser uses a larger minimum and rejects [OBJ-011](#obj-011). The packet remains valid under the defined object grammar. A11 discourages compressed objects/items on RF for interoperability; that is not a syntax deletion.

8. **Telemetry special sequence and extensions.** APRS101 p.68 explicitly permits `MIC` in the three-character sequence slot, with or without the following comma. FAP rejects that form. Both variants are retained in [TLM-004](#tlm-004) and [TLM-005](#tlm-005). Fractional, short, or undefined analog fields in FAP are outside the original five-byte-channel format. Definition messages target the station being described and need not be addressed to their sender.

9. **Message limits and acknowledgments.** APRS101 p.71 permits zero-length text and 1–5 alphanumeric ID characters. FAP rejects the empty message but also accepts several nonstandard lengths/bytes in its own fixtures. It recognizes ack/rej by a looser prefix rule; ordinary text such as `acknowledge this please` must not become an acknowledgment under the strict syntax. See [MSG-001](#msg-001) and [MSG-019](#msg-019).

10. **Reply acknowledgment.** The linked reply-ack scheme uses the legacy ID capacity for a two-character message number, `}`, and an optional two-character previous-message acknowledgment. Store those components separately. A standalone ack can echo the combined ID. Auto-answer messages have no new message ID; their optional terminal `}yy` acknowledges a previous message. The upstream permissive reply-ack fixtures do not enlarge the protocol's strict field limits. See [MSG-023](#msg-023) and [SEQ-003](#seq-003).

11. **Partial timestamps and status.** Partial APRS timestamps cannot supply an absolute date without a caller-supplied context and rollover policy. Only `DDHHMMz` is the status timestamp form in p.80; other timestamp-looking status text is preserved. FAP accepts some additional status forms and its raw-timestamp option does not behave uniformly for all packet categories. Host-clock-derived `Timestamp` values have therefore been excluded from compatibility assertions; explicit-date RMC values remain. See [TIM-019](#tim-019).

12. **Checksum versus fix validity.** The upstream GGA no-fix fixture has a bad checksum, so rejection alone cannot prove its fix-status check. [NME-014](#nme-014) uses status 0 and the correct `*4E` checksum. GLL/RMC invalid-status cases similarly have correct checksums. An implementation may expose the raw reported coordinates but must not update a trusted position from them.

13. **Historical X1J exception.** APRS101 allowed searching for `!` near the beginning of a non-APRS beacon; the live addendum deprecates this in 2012. Identical packets intentionally have separate historical and modern expectations. The pinned FAP fallback retains old behavior. See [OTH-035](#oth-035) and [OTH-036](#oth-036).

14. **Names, padding, and retained state.** Right-padded object names normalize for identity, but case and internal spaces remain significant. The names clarification disallows leading-space names; objects/items/stations participate in a shared naming model. Killed records remain available for later revival. FAP sometimes trims comments and consumes separators differently from the raw semantic contract. See [SEQ-002](#seq-002) and [SEQ-001](#seq-001).

15. **Weather field collisions and examples.** Lowercase `s` is wind speed in positionless weather and snowfall in complete weather. The linked WX prose confirms this but its snow examples inconsistently use uppercase `S`; the core cases follow lowercase `s` and do not silently accept both spellings as a normative rule. Lowercase `l123` means 1123 W/m². A raw rain counter has no universal precipitation conversion. Some p.66 examples are abbreviated or malformed; generated complete packets follow the grammar, not those omissions. The p.64 pressure row's byte count must include `b` plus five digits. See [WX-041](#wx-041).

16. **IGate capability notation.** APRS101 p.77 and FAP use `<` for capability announcements. The main A11 page's prose says “Left_bracket,” which is imprecise and conflicts with treating `[` as the obsolete grid DTI. The corpus follows the explicit `<` grammar, preserves capability token values, and does not invent a second `[IGate` grammar. See [QRY-018](#qry-018).

17. **Opaque and unsupported formats.** FAP rejection of a general query, VTG/WPL, a third-party packet, or a vendor variant is not sufficient reason to declare it malformed. Retain the appropriate specification or optional-capability case. Raw vendor formats without a supplied byte layout remain opaque instead of acquiring guessed sensor readings. Binary user-defined data is distinct from FAP's permissive handling of binary ordinary-message text. See [OTH-005](#oth-005).

18. **SSID and symbol interpretation.** Old source-SSID icon inference is isolated in the historical profile. Current SSID recommendations are usage hints, not a requirement to override an explicit information-field symbol. Destination-encoded symbols and the higher-priority body symbol are tested separately. Live TOCALL/product and symbol registries are not frozen by this corpus. See [NME-021](#nme-021).

Implementation references for the disagreements: [weather.go](https://github.com/hessu/go-aprs-fap/blob/94c7118ca94d251990382b9210112ddd5b260efa/weather.go), [mice.go](https://github.com/hessu/go-aprs-fap/blob/94c7118ca94d251990382b9210112ddd5b260efa/mice.go), [object.go](https://github.com/hessu/go-aprs-fap/blob/94c7118ca94d251990382b9210112ddd5b260efa/object.go), [telemetry.go](https://github.com/hessu/go-aprs-fap/blob/94c7118ca94d251990382b9210112ddd5b260efa/telemetry.go), [message.go](https://github.com/hessu/go-aprs-fap/blob/94c7118ca94d251990382b9210112ddd5b260efa/message.go), [timestamp.go](https://github.com/hessu/go-aprs-fap/blob/94c7118ca94d251990382b9210112ddd5b260efa/timestamp.go), and [nmea_test.go](https://github.com/hessu/go-aprs-fap/blob/94c7118ca94d251990382b9210112ddd5b260efa/nmea_test.go). These are pinned implementation evidence, not substitutes for the cited APRS grammar.

## HDR — TNC2 headers and transport

Envelope splitting; repeated markers; eight-hop boundary; destination dispatch; historical destination-SSID routing.

<a id="hdr-001"></a>

### HDR-001 — No digipeaters

```json
{
  "id": "HDR-001",
```

<a id="family-net"></a>

## NET — Third-party packets and network conventions

Third-party nested envelopes; no-gate/no-archive; q-token preservation; AEA adapter.

<a id="net-001"></a>

### NET-001 — Third-party message

```json
{
  "id": "NET-001",
  "title": "Third-party message",
  "profile": "core-1.1",
  "outcome": "accept",
  "source": "APRS101 pp. 83-86",
  "packet": "N0GATE>APRS,WIDE2-1:}W1AW>APRS,TCPIP,N0GATE*::N0CALL   :Hello{01",
  "expected": {
    "header": {
      "source": "N0GATE",
      "destination": "APRS",
      "path": [
        {
          "address": "WIDE2-1",
          "repeated_marker": false
        }
      ]
    },
    "kind": "third-party",
    "inner_packet": "W1AW>APRS,TCPIP,N0GATE*::N0CALL   :Hello{01",
    "inner": {
      "header": {
        "source": "W1AW",
        "destination": "APRS",
        "path": [
          {
            "address": "TCPIP",
            "repeated_marker": false
          },
          {
            "address": "N0GATE",
            "repeated_marker": true
          }
        ]
      },
      "kind": "message",
      "message": {
        "addressee": "N0CALL",
        "addressee_raw": "N0CALL   ",
        "text": "Hello",
        "message_id": "01",
        "ack_requested": true
      }
    },
    "message_origin": "W1AW"
  },
  "note": "The outer transmitter is N0GATE; the message origin and ack recipient are W1AW. Do not discard either envelope.",
  "packet_length_bytes": 64
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "NET-008",
  "title": "Preserve APRS-IS q token qAR",
  "profile": "aprs-is",
  "outcome": "accept",
  "source": "A11 APRS-IS; FAP aprsis_paths_test.go",
  "packet": "N0CALL>APRS,WIDE1-1,qAR,IGATE:>Ready",
  "expected": {
    "header": {
      "source": "N0CALL",
      "destination": "APRS",
      "path": [

          "repeated_marker": false
        },
        {
          "address": "qAR",
          "repeated_marker": false
        },
        {
          "address": "IGATE",
          "repeated_marker": false
        }
      ]

    "kind": "status",
    "status_text": "Ready",
    "aprs_is": {
      "q_construct_raw": "qAR",
      "following_path": ["IGATE"]
    }
  },
  "note": "q token case is significant. This case asserts preservation, not server-side q validation or RF address validity.",
  "packet_length_bytes": 36
}
```

<a id="family-seq"></a>

## SEQ — Stateful sequences

Object ownership/lifecycle; case/name identity; duplicate messages/reply-ack; telemetry calibration; bulletins; status precedence; weather association.

<a id="seq-001"></a>

### SEQ-001 — Object ownership, kill and revival

```json
{
```

```json
        "pending_reply_ack": "01"
      },

    }

  "note": "Receiver N0CALL has outbound message 02 pending. Deduplication uses sender + message ID/content, excluding the changing piggyback ACK; sending/retry timing is not executed by this corpus."
```

<a id="family-fap"></a>

## FAP — Pinned upstream compatibility corpus

Every captured root-parser invocation plus eligible full-packet/encoder/CLI supplements from the pinned tests.

### Compatibility schema and defaults

These rows preserve observed public packet fields from the pinned parser. `options` records the original root invocation settings; supplemental literal decodes used raw timestamps. `ax25` enables the parser's strict-address option; it does **not** change the input to binary AX.25. `accept_broken_mice` selects FAP's mangled-byte recovery.

Expand the following top-level defaults into `expected.fap_fields`, then overlay the case's explicit fields. Nested `Message`, `Wx`, and telemetry objects retain their captured nulls/empty strings. `SymbolTable`, `SymbolCode`, and `DaoDatumByte` are displayed as one-byte strings (or null for zero) instead of Go integer byte values. `fap_header` contains normalized source/destination and the parser's digipeater interpretation, which can differ from explicit marker preservation in core cases.

```json
{
  "fap_field_defaults": {
    "Type": "",
    "Format": "",
    "Latitude": null,
    "Longitude": null,
    "PosAmbiguity": null,
    "PosResolution": null,
    "SymbolTable": null,
    "SymbolCode": null,
    "Speed": null,
    "Course": null,
    "Altitude": null,
    "Messaging": null,
    "PHG": "",
    "RadioRange": null,
    "RawTimestamp": "",
    "ObjectName": "",
    "ItemName": "",
    "Alive": null,
    "Message": null,
    "Status": "",
    "Wx": null,
    "TelemetryData": null,
    "Capabilities": null,
    "MBits": "",
    "MiceMangled": false,
    "DaoDatumByte": null,
    "GPSFixStatus": null,
    "ChecksumOK": null,
    "Comment": "",
    "Warnings": null
  }
}
```

`Timestamp` has no implicit assertion when absent: host-derived values are deliberately excluded. When present for RMC, its complete date comes from that sentence and the pinned implementation's year interpretation. `OrigPacket`, `Header`, and `Body` are omitted because they are derivable from the exact input. On failure, `fap_error` is the observed error text; other fields are the partial result that FAP returned. A different implementation should normally compare an error category rather than reproduce that text.

FAP units: `Latitude`/`Longitude` degrees; `PosResolution` meters; `Speed` km/h; `Course` degrees; `Altitude` meters; `RadioRange` km. Weather `WindSpeed`/`WindGust` use m/s, `Temp`/`TempIn` Celsius, pressure millibars (hPa), rain/snow mm, humidity percent, luminosity W/m², water level meters, radiation nSv/hour, and battery voltage V. See the [public structs](https://github.com/hessu/go-aprs-fap/blob/94c7118ca94d251990382b9210112ddd5b260efa/fap.go). The FAP nested field names are intentionally unchanged.

Every root `Parse` invocation captured during the test run is represented, including repeated inputs with different options and all 227 binary-message cases. This is a complete capture of those exercised parser invocations, not every helper-only input, benchmark iteration, encoder source coordinate, or fuzzer-generated possibility. Encoder expected bodies appear with a documented synthetic envelope so they can serve as full decoding fixtures.
